The Stair to the Heavens
A stair of cloud and gold, up to the Heavens, where every power the Atlas knows now keeps a palace in their own country. Walk up the steps, or press E at the gate.
Free to everyone: the reading room, the stacks, the children's corner and the papers.
The city's own collections: galleries, a great hall and a café. Free on every day of the week.
Films every evening, matinées at the weekend; the foyer bar is open all day.
Rooms by the night or the week, a dining room and a bar; the doorman will take your bags.
A park: lawns, a bandstand, flower beds and shade. The gates are never locked.
A square for everyone: the fountain, the market stalls, the buskers and somewhere to sit.
Swings, slides and the climbing frame, and the splash pad's fountains in summer. Grown-ups sit on the benches.
Clipped hedges, roses in their beds and a long still pool. Quiet, please, for the birds.
The open-air pool: fifty metres of warm blue water, the diving board, loungers and parasols, and the Lido Café. Press E at the water's edge to swim a length.
